correctness.rationale: For divisor p|a, m=a/p>=2, gcd(a,d)=1, odd q between 3 and a-1, coin offsets 1,3,...,q, the least number of offset coins at x=uq+v (1<=v<=q) is u+1+1_{v even}. Capacity and parity show this for all x; the inequalities lambda(x+2)>=lambda(x) and lambda(x+a)>=lambda(x) for a>q justify minimal quotient Apéry representatives w_{dr}=hm lambda(pr)+dr. They strictly increase along r by steps of 2, so only final/penultimate residues compete; comparing t=a-p-q floor((a-p-1)/q) yields F=B+1_{p,t odd, t>p} max(hm-d,0). Boundary m=2 has no penultimate admissible candidate and no correction; p=1 allowed. Fresh independent Dijkstra shortest-residue calculations match examples (12,3,2,1,9)->14, (15,3,4,2,11)->43, (20,4,1,3,13)->17. Pinned verify_exact.py is an independent broader Dijkstra implementation but its saved 125586-case log was not used as infinite proof.
